brief.headline: Lock better payment terms and a modest price cut — you're 1.36% of their sales, they carry debt 2.25× equity and need cash flow

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 3–5% price cut on Dextrose to align with the India export benchmark and strengthen our cost position
priceAsk.target: Target ₹63–64/KG (from current ₹66.48/KG), moving closer to the ₹42.95/kg India export line and the lower end of the ₹60–81/kg market band
priceAsk.basis: Our ₹66.48/KG sits in the 'MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable)' zone but well above the ₹42.95/kg export benchmark; the typical ask band is ₹66–73/kg, so we have room to press down while staying commercial

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (move from 30 days to 15 days after receipt) in exchange for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: This costs us ₹61.76 L in cash we'd otherwise hold — use that as trade: they get cash 15 days sooner, we get the lower price

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji is big (₹1102.11 Cr revenue) but financially stretched — they keep only 2.3% profit and owe 2.25× their own cash (₹238.85 Cr total debt). Their health score is D (21/100), meaning tight finances. You are 1.36% of everything they sell (₹15.03 Cr), so you matter to them. They need reliable cash more than a deep margin, so trade faster payment for a price cut — it's worth real money to a supplier carrying that much debt. Don't squeeze so hard you risk supply, but do lean on the fact that keeping a ₹15 Cr customer happy is worth a few percentage points.

evidence.point: You are a significant customer to them
evidence.figure: Your ₹15.03 Cr is 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr revenue

evidence.point: They have very thin profit — only ₹2.30 kept for every ₹100 sold
They carry heavy debt relative to their own money
Our price is in the fair zone but above the export benchmark
evidence.figure: We pay ₹66.48/KG; India export line ₹42.95/kg; market ask ₹60–81/kg, verdict MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable)

evidence.point: Paying 15 days faster frees up cash for them
evidence.figure: Moving from 30 days to 15 days releases ₹61.76 L for us — worth that to them in earlier cash

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker with revenue ₹2359.06 Cr and health B (62/100) — a much stronger balance sheet and established dextrose/sorbitol supplier, direct drop-in alternate

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore maize wet-miller (₹365.39 Cr revenue) making Dextrose ANHYDROUS IV-fluid grade — exact form match, though health is also D (27/100); confirm IP monograph CoA before switching

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (₹821.13 Cr revenue, health C 53/100) with growing dextrose capacity — a credible second source to test

risks: Their 2.3% profit margin and D health score mean pushing too hard on price could destabilise supply — balance the ask with faster payment to keep them viable
We already pay the best price we've seen (₹66.48/KG across our suppliers), so any cut needs a clear trade (payment terms) and a credible alternate lined up
Debt at 2.25× equity is high but not crisis-level; still, watch for any delivery slips or quality issues that signal cash stress — have Gulshan or Sanstar ready to quote if needed

The market ask verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable)' — we're not overpaying badly, so frame the ask as aligning to the export benchmark and rewarding them with faster cash, not as fixing a major problem
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership — you're our lead Dextrose supplier at ₹15 Cr a year — and we'd like to lock that in by moving closer to the ₹42.95/kg export benchmark in exchange for paying you 15 days faster, putting cash in your hands sooner.
